description_raw: We designed the internal layout to make the most of spectacular views at Villa Ginestre, a newly built property located on the edge of Italy’s Lake Como. The stunning views across the water inspired us to play with sumptuous colours and textures to give the villa the luxurious feel that its location commands. We used fluted timber joinery and striped terrazzo flooring throughout the home, using a base of natural tones complemented by pops of colour and visually arresting bursts of pattern that surprise and challenge.

Perched on the edge of the Chastleton Estate in the Cotswolds, Glebe Cottage enjoys an idyllic rural setting. We gave the dilapidated cottage a thorough revamp, reconfiguring the layout to work for modern living. The new open plan kitchen and family dining room have given the property a new lease of life. We were careful to blend the contemporary layout with all the charm that a country cottage deserves, layering woods in different tones and finishes with rich, natural hues of brown, beige, green, blue and the deepest of reds. Carefully introduced textures and patterns played a key role throughout the property, from pretty wallpapers for the bedrooms to statement lamps, lightshades, vases and more. At Chastje in Latvia, we created an incredible educational, creative space to take children’s minds on an adventure. We transformed a huge barn into a multi-zoned space providing a journey through different worlds. Chastje draws influences from magical adventures and journeys as diverse as Narnia, the Orient Express, Around the World in 80 Days and the eccentric, uniquely visual narrative films of Wes Anderson. Zones include interactive game and learning areas, a waterplay zone, an activity space, a cinema, a music room/studio, an arts and crafts area, a science lab, an interactive maze, a family zone and more. One of the highlights is the fully immersive rainbow tunnel, which runs between the family room and the activity zone. The walls and floor of the glass tunnel are all interactive, enveloping children within a magical travelling experience as they pass through the space. The result of all of this is a world of mystery and discovery that invites an eagerness to learn and to enjoy every moment of the experience at Chastje.

With recent graduates in the spotlight as the target age group, and the name bringing to mind Anne Bancroft and Dustin Hoffman’s stellar performances in The Robinson is anything but conventional. Polite irreverence was a cornerstone of our conceptual design, as was that ‘look at me’ selfie focus that pervades the social media accounts of our target age group. Irony, satire, sarcasm and British eccentricity and wit shine through every element of the building. You can feel this spirit the moment you set foot through the over-large, metal panel front doors (with knockers peppering the inside) of the super lobby and into Wonderland. Timber panelling provides a sense of familiarity and comfort, along with wallpaper that would be at home in your grandma’s house, overlaid with translucent curtains that create a sense of theatre and possibility. Against this backdrop, the eye-blinding baby pink post room, Paul Smith-style striped post boxes with Dr Martens feet and floating chairs serve to contradict and challenge the senses, creating just that sense of wonder and curiosity that Alice felt when she plunged down the rabbit hole. We took the excitement to the next level with the addition of a giant mirror ball, which spins and refracts light around the lobby to toy with the senses in sparkling new ways. Procuring a mirror ball of that scale was no easy feat but we knew precisely the impact that it would deliver! We installed massive speakers in the super lobby, as well as on the rooftop and in the podium garden, so that music flows around the residents as they move throughout the development. Within each apartment, the design of the living space is quite simple and classic, but we used colour to spice it up and create something special. Kitchens range from turquoise to chilli red. Ceilings are exposed concrete with galvanised piping for a raw feeling. Lighting comes in coloured metal or bamboo. Wardrobes are covered by industrial-style curtains instead of doors. Bathrooms are super simple, with a black/white, Yin and Yang design and unexpected touches, such as the plus and minus signs on taps and the bespoke, handmade Liberty pattern lampshades for wit and contrast. Even the corridors feed that sense of the unexpected, from their bright colours and Caribbean-style patterned carpets to the individually painted front doors in differing colours. All with grandma-style wired lampshades floating above. The smaller lobbies mirror the timber panelling of the super lobby, while also featuring fringed pendant lights, contrasting coloured wallpaper and concrete benches with bright coloured cushions. With influences from , we’ve used a pick-and-mix design style to give these smaller lobbies their own unique character, while still fitting into the overall feel of The Robinson. The residents’ lounge is another very special space. The arrival hall includes a multi-layered art wall, along with an incredibly long bank of brightly coloured seats (we were aiming for the longest in London), with portholes overlooking a mini courtyard. Designed for working and socialising, the residents’ lounge features a Damien Hirst-inspired taxi coffee machine, complete with refrigerated section in the bonnet for those who want to chill a few beers. It’s a gathering place that’s brimming over with unexpected elements – the ultimate selfie spot in a building that’s already packed to the rafters with outstanding selfie spots. There’s a dining room within the residents’ lounge, as well as a kitchen for getting together to cook. Work pods and private booths for phone calls allow residents to use the space for professional purposes too. Of course, all work and no play makes for a dull building, so residents walking out of the work pods simply have to look through the enormous glass panes to see the courtyard space complete with slide to get from one level down to the next. The residents’ lounge, in keeping with the rest of The Robinson, is all about homely touches blended with unexpected quirks. We were delighted to source a 19 century, arched Rococo style, giltwood wall mirror, for example, to sit above a glass-backed fireplace. We replaced the glass so that residents can look through the mirror – as well as through the fireplace – as it frames the incredible view of London spread out below. The whole development is unapologetic in its creativity and sense of fun, both inside and out (click here to discover the Robinson’s external spaces, from the Mad Hatter’s Tea Party Garden to the rooftop slide). It inspires curiosity at every turn, with a sense of humour and belonging that encourages residents to express themselves and enjoy every moment.

Making the most of the beautiful high ceilings and large windows, we chose elegant, natural tones that work with the luminous interior of Cadogan Square. Serene creams, browns and greys provide the perfect backdrop for a few statement items that use purple to deliver a rich warmth. Lighting is bold and exciting, introducing golden tones that are mirrored in subtle touches elsewhere, while contrasting beautifully with the cool marble of the bathroom and fireplaces. Patterns and textures are used playfully, from the circular metal maps on the wall to the shimmer of the headboard that stretches all the way to the ceiling. Elegant with bold touches, the overall feel is classic yet contemporary.

We’ve layered textures to beautiful effect in this home, all the way from the plush rug underfoot to the cascading glass of the pendant lights. Smooth polished wood reflects the light, with light beiges and creams offsetting the darker tones. We’ve used marble in the kitchen, for the fireplace and extensively in the bathroom alongside wood for a natural flow throughout. Statement chairs invite rest and relaxation, while coloured cushions, vases and other objects add interest and depth.

In the heart of Knightsbridge, Ennismore Gardens exudes luxury. We layered textures, from cool marble to polished woods to the softest of deep pile carpets. The home is packed with modern, urban touches, from statement furniture pieces to exciting lighting to a temperature-controlled wine room – everything a well-to-do Londoner could possibly desire.

The iconic Notting Hill location set the tone for our work at St Lukes Mews for the outset. Tasked with finding a property for an international investor, we collaborated with the developer to manage this project from start to finish. Refined yet cosy, this is chic urban living at its very best. We took a creative approach to the space, designing it with a contemporary London couple in mind. We turned the home upside down, putting the living space and open plan kitchen at the top of the house and expanding the roof terrace. We turned the first floor into a huge main bedroom suite, layering colours and textures to deliver a cocoon of luxury in this leading London location.
